bodies.subject: Are you the bottleneck?
bodies.note: Testimonial email. The lesson is genuinely useful and complete on its own; the workshop is only in the P.S.
bodies.body:
After coming to the workshop...

Rhys was able to buy back his time and focus on higher leverage work.

(Instead of putting out fires all day).

Watch his review here

Here's how he did it: he removed himself as the constraint.

This business owner was taking all the sales calls because he was the best closer. Sound familiar?

In doing so, he didn't realize he had become the bottleneck.

Many founders fall into this trap...

Believing no one can sell as well as they can.

But this way of thinking creates a ceiling on both your income and sales.

If you're taking most of the calls because you have the highest close rate, you might be the constraint in your business.

It's not a skill problem, it's a people problem.

The fix?

Bring in more closers and open up your calendar availability.

Yes, close rates may dip (for a moment), but you can counteract that with training.

The key is that your business can now handle more calls and make more money.

Plus, as an entrepreneur, you free yourself up to grow other areas of the business.

Remove yourself as the constraint.

- Alex

PS - Finding the right candidate isn't easy. But doing so is crucial to removing yourself from the day-to-day operations.

At our workshops we provide strategies for identifying and eliminating constraints as well as effective hiring.

Discover if you're a fit for our workshops here

bodies.subject: Here's Your Scaling Roadmap (Stage 4)
bodies.note: Day 1 of the stage-segmented sequence. The lead magnet is chosen by YOUR stage, not sent blind.
bodies.body:
As promised, here is your Scaling Roadmap:

Tap below for your PDF:

>> SCALING ROADMAP - STAGE 4 <<

Inside you'll find a PDF and video going over…

- Exactly what Stage 4 is and the constraints you may be facing

- Possible solutions to those constraints

- And what it takes to advance to Stage 5

Note: The PDF contains links to the videos and downloads that correspond to them.

Stage 4 is when you go from being a “trainer” to becoming a real “manager.”

At 5-9 employees, you will have your first real team with one layer of organization between you and the front-line workers.

The big difference is that you can't do everything anymore…

You have to do what matters most.

The main problem at Stage 4 is that you have been saying “yes” to any customer who would pay you.

Now that is causing problems because different customers want different things.

You need to figure out who your best customers are and focus on them.

The roadmap linked here email lays out what you need to do next.

Enjoy,

P.S. A lot of businesses at this stage do lots of activity and they don't grow because they're solving the wrong problems - for the wrong person.

bodies.subject: You can't do everything anymore
bodies.note: Day 2. Pure symptom list. Every bullet is a thing a Stage 4 owner is feeling right now, and it ends on a cliffhanger for day 3.
bodies.body:
You are in Stage 4 of our Scaling Roadmap.

(If you haven't opened your Stage 4 PDF yet, open it by clicking here.)

You've got 5-9 employees, and your role has changed from "trainer" to becoming a real "manager."

You can't do everything anymore - you have to choose what matters most.

At this stage, you may be noticing the following…

- You've said yes to anyone who would pay, and now your product is pulled in too many directions

- You're getting too many unqualified leads (people who aren't right for your business)

- You have no way to measure if customers are happy

- Your new team isn't using all your tools properly

- You're wasting time interviewing people who aren't right for the job

- You keep getting surprised by “one-time” expenses

Here's your job at this stage:

Make the business more focused and professional.

Here's what you need to do to graduate from Stage 4:

Choose Your Focus: Figure out who your best customers are. Change your product to serve them better. Say “no” to customers who are not a good fit.

Get Organized: Add simple rules and policies so work stays consistent. Set up proper systems for tracking sales. Keep customer info in one place. Make sure everyone uses the same tools.

Start Measuring Things: Know your numbers. Track how many leads turn into sales. Measure customer satisfaction. Watch the basic money numbers so you know what is working.

Make Things Professional: Run the business like a real company. Write an employee handbook. Get proper insurance. Create basic processes for everything.

I know that may sound like a lot.

Start with identifying and prioritizing your best kind of customers.

This will make your sales smoother and delivery more efficient.

Tomorrow, I will show you the 80/20 customer audit I use to identify exactly who you should target.

Serve the best. Ignore the rest.

- Alex

P.S - I talk about this in-depth in the training course provided in your Stage 4 Scaling Roadmap. You can watch it here.

bodies.subject: Say no. Win bigger.
bodies.note: Day 3. One complete, do-it-today tactic given away free, with a per-department checklist attached. The pitch is four words in the P.S.
bodies.body:
Yesterday, I showed you what you need to graduate from Stage 4.

(If you haven't opened your Stage 4 PDF yet, open it by clicking here.)

The main problem at Stage 4 is that you've been saying “yes” to any customer who would pay you.

Now that's causing problems because different customers want different things.

You need to figure out who your best customers are and focus on them.

The Solution: The 80/20 Customer Audit

In most businesses, 80% of customers take up the most headaches and resources. While also giving the lowest return.

The top 20% are the ones to replicate.

They pay more. They complain less. They take less effort to fulfill. They get better results. They refer more often.

When you isolate your best customers, you'll see a pattern.

They tend to share the same type of business and they need the same type of delivery.

Those top 20% customers are what you're going to build the business around.

Do this:

Open a sheet and list every customer from the last 12 months.

Give each customer a ranking of 1-10 on each of the following:

- Total revenue paid
- Ease of fulfillment
- Satisfaction with your service

Sort by revenue and write down what the top customers have in common (industry, size, urgency, use case, outcome).

Pay close attention to the ones with high revenue, low ease of fulfilment, and high satisfaction with your service.

Those are the customers you need to clone.

Your job is to get more customers exactly like them and optimize your product around that type of customer.

That is your focus this week…

Bonus: Stage 4 Wins By Department

Product: Specialize product and price to serve your niched down avatar.
Marketing: Make better free stuff and add more creatives to boost volume.
Sales: Track basic KPIs manually on a spreadsheet.
Customer Service: Install tracking & KPIs and centralize notes for each customer by getting a basic CRM.
IT: Get everyone on platforms. Protect passwords. Get a project management tool and a work chat tool.
Recruiting: Learn how to screen and conduct a 2-step interview process.
HR: Create an employee handbook and policies.
Finance: Get profit and loss statements set up. Get basic insurance.

I talk about this all in-depth in the training course provided in your Stage 4 Scaling Roadmap.

You can watch it here.

Go after the 20%,

- Alex

P.S. If you want our help to select the right avatar, you can grab a seat at one of our next available workshops.

bodies.subject: Supply or Demand?
bodies.note: Setter re-engagement, fired off CONTENT CONSUMPTION not a form fill. Plain text, no links, one binary question, reply asked for.
bodies.body:
Will , saw you were going through some of Alex and Leila's resources recently.

Quick question: is it a Supply problem or a Demand problem?

Supply = you can't deliver more. Everything runs through you. We'd need to build the right team and streamline your systems and processes to scale.

Demand = you can't sell enough. There's not enough leads or the leads aren't converting. We'd need to refine your marketing, offer, or sales process to sign more customers.

Reply with which one resonates, and I'll send over resources to solve this constraint for businesses like yours.

P.S. YES I'm a real human haha

-Ronney M.
